payload.purpose: Saturday 10:00 to 1:00 for people whose week has no room.

captions.LI:
Many people tell us they need support but their weekday schedule is packed.

That's why the Bariatric Counseling Center runs a Saturday track from 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., both onsite and virtual. It's the same comprehensive program, behavioral therapy, dietary guidance, culinary classes, and mindful movement. One program, not four.

Saturday sessions are part of our Intensive Outpatient Program, which runs about three months and roughly 30 sessions. Patients typically attend for little to no cost, as claims are processed under mental health benefits and we're in-network with most health insurance plans.

If your week has no room, your weekend does. San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

#BehavioralHealth

payload.title: Mon 12/14: Sleep and appetite
payload.purpose: Short nights and the next day's eating. Repurposes the site article; plain, no numbers.

captions.FB:
Sleep and appetite are more connected than most people realize.

Short nights can shift the next day's eating in ways that feel automatic. You might notice stronger cravings, less satisfaction from meals, or feeling hungry soon after eating.

This isn't a willpower issue. When sleep is cut short, the body's hunger signals change. The systems that tell you when you've had enough don't work the same way.

At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we look at patterns like this as part of a bigger picture. Sleep, stress, eating rhythms, and daily routines all affect each other. Understanding these connections makes it easier to respond in ways that actually help.

If you're noticing patterns you'd like to change, our team is here. We work with clients in San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

Link in the first comment.

payload.title: Tue 12/22: Referring providers: weight loss medications and the behavioral half
payload.purpose: Patients on weight loss medications (never the drug class abbreviation): the habits that keep the result. Document post.

captions.LI: Patients on weight loss medications often see remarkable physical results, but long-term success depends on the behavioral half of treatment. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we provide the structure patients need to build sustainable habits around food, movement, and self-care. Our Intensive Outpatient Program runs about three months and roughly 30 sessions, meeting 2 to 3 times per week, serving patients both onsite at the state-of-the-art San Antonio facility and virtually throughout Texas. The staff is comprised of a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, registered dietitians, movement therapists, and a registered nurse, as well as a professional chef. The program can be standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medication that patients receive from their medical providers. Our team coordinates care with referring medical providers and, at patient discharge, we give referring providers a detailed summary of the patient's behavioral progress during the time in our intensive outpatient program. Progress notes as requested, typically within two business days. We accept most health insurances. Our Director of Admissions is Leloni Gonzales at lgonzales@bccsanantonio.com and 210-634-2200. #BehavioralHealth
